questions.question: Who painted "The Starry Night"?
questions.fact: Van Gogh painted "The Starry Night" in 1889 from his room at an asylum in Saint-Rémy, France. He sold very few paintings in his lifetime.

questions.question: Which Spanish artist painted "Guernica"?
questions.fact: "Guernica" is almost 8 metres wide. Picasso painted it in 1937 after the bombing of the Basque town.

questions.question: Which surrealist painted melting clocks in "The Persistence of Memory"?
questions.fact: Dalí said the melting clocks were inspired by a Camembert cheese softening in the sun.

questions.question: Who wrote "Don Quixote"?
questions.fact: Cervantes and Shakespeare both died around 23 April 1616 (by different calendars), which is why 23 April is World Book Day.

questions.question: Who wrote "Romeo and Juliet"?
questions.fact: Romeo and Juliet is set in Verona, Italy, where tourists visit "Juliet's balcony" today.

questions.question: Which Madrid museum houses "Las Meninas"?
questions.fact: The Prado opened in 1819 and holds one of the greatest collections of European paintings in the world.

questions.question: Who painted "Las Meninas"?
questions.fact: Velázquez painted himself into "Las Meninas", standing at his easel on the left.

questions.question: Where is Picasso's "Guernica" on display today?
questions.fact: Guernica only came to Spain in 1981. Picasso had said it should not go there until democracy returned.

questions.question: Which architect designed Barcelona's Sagrada Família?
questions.fact: Gaudí is buried in the crypt of the Sagrada Família. Seven of his works are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.

questions.question: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
questions.fact: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling standing on scaffolding, over about four years.

questions.question: Who wrote the Harry Potter books?
questions.fact: J.K. Rowling's first Harry Potter book was rejected by 12 publishers before one said yes.

questions.question: Who wrote "The Lord of the Rings"?
questions.fact: Tolkien invented whole languages for his elves, and wrote the stories partly to give them a world to live in.

questions.question: Which author created Sherlock Holmes?
questions.fact: Conan Doyle was a doctor. He based Sherlock Holmes partly on one of his university teachers, Dr Joseph Bell.

questions.question: What is the name of Agatha Christie's famous Belgian detective?
questions.fact: Agatha Christie is the best-selling novelist of all time, with billions of copies sold.

questions.question: Who wrote "One Hundred Years of Solitude"?
questions.fact: García Márquez won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1982. The novel is set in the made-up town of Macondo.

questions.question: Who wrote "1984"?
questions.fact: George Orwell's real name was Eric Blair. "1984" gave us terms like "Big Brother" and "thoughtcrime".

questions.question: Who painted "The Scream"?
questions.fact: Munch made several versions of "The Scream", in paint and pastel, and two of them were stolen and recovered.

questions.question: Which Austrian painter made "The Kiss", full of gold?
questions.fact: Klimt used real gold leaf in "The Kiss", which hangs in the Belvedere museum in Vienna.

questions.question: Claude Monet is famous for paintings of…
questions.fact: Monet painted about 250 paintings of the water lilies in his own garden at Giverny.

questions.question: Andy Warhol famously painted cans of which soup brand?
questions.fact: Warhol said he ate Campbell's soup for lunch almost every day for 20 years.

questions.question: Which art movement did Picasso help start?
questions.fact: Cubism shows objects from several angles at once, broken into geometric shapes.

questions.question: Which Catalan artist's colourful style has stars and moons, with a foundation in Barcelona?
questions.fact: Miró designed the logo of Spain's tourism board, the colourful sun still used today.

questions.question: In which town is the Dalí Theatre-Museum?
questions.fact: Dalí is buried in a crypt under the stage of his own museum in Figueres.

questions.question: Which museum in Bilbao has a famous titanium building by Frank Gehry?
questions.fact: The Guggenheim Bilbao opened in 1997 and transformed the city. Experts even call it the "Bilbao effect".

questions.question: Which museum holds the Mona Lisa?
questions.fact: The Louvre is the most visited museum in the world. It was once a royal palace.

questions.question: Who wrote "Pride and Prejudice"?
questions.fact: Jane Austen published her novels anonymously; "Pride and Prejudice" was credited to "the author of Sense and Sensibility".

questions.question: Who wrote "Frankenstein"?
questions.fact: Mary Shelley started writing Frankenstein at 18, during a ghost-story contest with friends at Lake Geneva.

questions.question: Who wrote "Dracula"?
questions.fact: Bram Stoker never visited Transylvania. He researched it in libraries.

questions.question: Which novel begins with "Call me Ishmael"?
options: The Old Man and the Sea
questions.fact: Moby-Dick was a commercial flop when it came out in 1851. Today it's called one of the greatest American novels.

questions.question: Who wrote "The Little Prince"?
questions.fact: The Little Prince is one of the most translated books in the world, into hundreds of languages.

questions.question: Who wrote "Les Misérables"?
questions.fact: Les Misérables became one of the longest-running musicals ever, first staged in English in London in 1985.

questions.question: Who wrote "Around the World in Eighty Days"?
questions.fact: Jules Verne also wrote "Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Seas" and is one of the most translated authors ever.

questions.question: Which Spanish poet wrote "Romancero gitano" and "The House of Bernarda Alba"?
questions.fact: Lorca was killed early in the Spanish Civil War in 1936; his body has never been found.

questions.question: Which Barcelona novel by Carlos Ruiz Zafón features the Cemetery of Forgotten Books?
questions.fact: The Shadow of the Wind is one of the best-selling Spanish novels of all time and starts a series of four books.

questions.question: Who sculpted the famous marble "David" in Florence's Accademia?
questions.fact: Michelangelo's David is over 5 metres tall and was carved from a single block of marble.

questions.question: Who sculpted "The Thinker"?
questions.fact: "The Thinker" was first meant to show the poet Dante, as part of a giant gateway called "The Gates of Hell".

questions.question: Which Dutch painter made "Girl with a Pearl Earring"?
questions.fact: Very little is known about Vermeer's life, and only around 35 of his paintings survive.

questions.question: Which Spanish painter made "The Third of May 1808"?
questions.fact: Goya painted it in 1814 about Napoleon's troops executing Spanish civilians in Madrid. It hangs in the Prado.

questions.question: Which Valencian painter is famous for sunny beach scenes?
questions.fact: Sorolla painted over 2,000 works. His house in Madrid is now the Museo Sorolla.

questions.question: Which painter was born in Crete and worked in Toledo?
questions.fact: El Greco means "the Greek". His real name was Domenikos Theotokopoulos.

questions.question: Who wrote "The Old Man and the Sea"?
questions.fact: Hemingway won the Pulitzer Prize for "The Old Man and the Sea" and loved Spain, especially Pamplona's San Fermín.

questions.question: Who wrote "The Great Gatsby"?
questions.fact: The Great Gatsby sold poorly while Fitzgerald was alive. Today it sells hundreds of thousands of copies a year.

questions.question: Who wrote "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory"?
questions.fact: As a schoolboy, Roald Dahl tested new chocolate bars for Cadbury, which inspired the book.

questions.question: Who wrote "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland"?
questions.fact: Lewis Carroll's real name was Charles Dodgson, and he was a maths teacher at Oxford University.

questions.question: Who wrote "Peter Pan"?
questions.fact: J.M. Barrie gave the rights to Peter Pan to a children's hospital in London, Great Ormond Street.

questions.question: Who wrote "Winnie-the-Pooh"?
questions.fact: Winnie-the-Pooh was named after Winnipeg, a real black bear at London Zoo that Milne's son Christopher Robin loved to visit.

questions.question: George R.R. Martin's book series that became "Game of Thrones" is called…
options: A Song of Ice and Fire
questions.fact: George R.R. Martin has been writing the sixth book, "The Winds of Winter", for many years. Fans are still waiting.

questions.question: Who wrote "The Hunger Games"?
questions.fact: Suzanne Collins said the idea came while flipping between a reality TV show and news footage of war.

questions.question: Which Brazilian author wrote "The Alchemist"?
questions.fact: The Alchemist was first published in 1988 and has been translated into more than 80 languages.

questions.question: What are the three traditional primary colours in painting?
questions.fact: Printers and screens use different primaries: cyan, magenta and yellow for ink; red, green and blue for light.

questions.question: What do you get when you mix red and white paint?
questions.fact: "Pink" was first used as a colour name in the late 1600s, after a flower called the pink.

questions.question: Which painting style uses tiny dots of colour, like Seurat's?
questions.fact: Seurat's "A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte" took about two years to paint, dot by dot.

questions.question: Banksy is famous for which kind of art?
questions.fact: Banksy's real identity is still officially unknown. In 2018 one of his paintings shredded itself right after being sold at auction.

questions.question: Who painted "The Birth of Venus"?
questions.fact: Botticelli painted "The Birth of Venus" in the 1480s. It hangs in the Uffizi Gallery in Florence.

questions.question: Which Mexican artist is famous for self-portraits with flowers in her hair?
questions.fact: Frida Kahlo painted around 55 self-portraits, many while recovering from a serious bus accident.

questions.question: How many lines does a sonnet have?
questions.fact: Shakespeare wrote 154 sonnets. Sonnet 18 begins "Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?"

questions.question: Who wrote "The Odyssey"?
questions.fact: The Odyssey follows Odysseus's ten-year journey home after the Trojan War, and is nearly 3,000 years old.

questions.question: Who wrote "The Divine Comedy"?
questions.fact: The Divine Comedy has three parts: Inferno, Purgatorio and Paradiso. It helped shape the modern Italian language.

questions.question: Which Shakespeare play has the line "To be, or not to be"?
questions.fact: Hamlet is Shakespeare's longest play.

questions.question: Who wrote "The Da Vinci Code"?
questions.fact: The Da Vinci Code has sold over 80 million copies and was filmed with Tom Hanks.

questions.question: Which author wrote "It" and "The Shining"?
questions.fact: Stephen King has written more than 60 novels, many set in his home state of Maine.

questions.question: What colour do you get by mixing blue and red paint?
questions.fact: Purple dye was once so expensive that it became the colour of emperors and kings.
